name: Decisioncraft
title: Decisioncraft | Amplifier Smart Tools
promise: Decide together, with every voice in the room.
description: Map how a problem works today and what you plan to change. Put the evidence beside every claim, gather notes from every point of view, and leave the review with a short, ranked list of what to decide.
alt: A bakery's decision about a monthly box: the list of views on the left, a subscriber's journey on the map, a walk-through card, a step's notes with an answer, and the questions to decide.
caption: Screen recording of the bakery example: take the walk-through, open a step, answer a question, then see everything that needs deciding.
flow_intro: Start from the notes, interviews, data or code you already have. Decisioncraft turns them into one map that a mixed group can read without training.
steps: Give your agent the material: meeting notes, interviews, figures, documents. It drafts a decision model with sources, quoted evidence, journeys or stages, and gaps between today and the plan.
Designers, analysts, engineers, owners, security, the people you serve, an AI agent teammate and finance each leave notes. Every note ends in a question.
Send one offline file round. Reviewers take the walk-through, answer questions, place dots on what matters most and save their answers. Merge the answers to see where people agree.
detail_title: Keep the reasons with the decision.
details: Boxes and notes link to the exact words or numbers behind them, with the source and date. Customer and patient quotes are marked as their own words.
Differences between today and the plan become gaps with user stories, done-when checks, and impact and effort scores. Quick wins sort to the top.
Compare two versions of a model before a follow-up review. New and changed boxes are marked, and boxes not checked for a while say so.
prompt: Use Decisioncraft to help us decide whether to open on Sundays. Read decisioncraft --help, draft a model from the notes in ./notes with the customer-journey template, check it with validate, then render the canvas and open it for review.
prerequisites: Python 3.11 or later. Canvases are single HTML files that open in any current browser, offline.
model_note: Drafting a model and adding role notes need separately configured Anthropic or OpenAI access. Checking, drawing, comparing and merging reviews need no model.

capability_demos.title: A bakery weighs a monthly box.
capability_demos.description: Three shops, customer chats, 64 survey slips, a waste log and the till supplier's notes. Six journeys follow a subscriber's month and the work behind the counter, then trace the idea from what customers said to a pilot plan.
capability_demos.alt: The bakery example: a customer journey across five phases, with notes counted on each step.
capability_demos.caption: Screen recording. Fictional business, people and figures.

capability_demos.title: A web team moves its file uploads.
capability_demos.description: An incident review, a month of upload numbers, support tickets and a new provider's terms. Six journeys show uploads, downloads, deletes, a file move and failures across the system, with an options tree beside them.
capability_demos.alt: The uploads example: two journeys across customer, web app, servers, database, background jobs and storage.
capability_demos.caption: Screen recording. Fictional team and figures.

capability_demos.title: A town decides on a footbridge.
capability_demos.description: An inspection, crossing counts, an access audit, quotes for a way across and a shops survey. The canvas traces the decision, compares three options from committee to reopening, and follows a resident through a closure.
capability_demos.alt: The footbridge example: a decision chain from source to outcome, with planned items marked by dashed borders.
capability_demos.caption: Screen recording. Fictional bridge, council and figures.

capability_demos.title: A ward changes how it sends people home.
capability_demos.description: A worked example about how a ward organises its work, not medical advice. Seven journeys follow a patient and carer home and the ward's evening list, medicines, discharge day and follow-up calls. Everything is invented.
capability_demos.alt: The ward example: a patient's journey home, today and with the proposed changes.
capability_demos.caption: Screen recording. Invented data; no real patients.
